bull_case: 유리한 사업·자본배분 가정이 유지되면 기준 점수보다 높은 결과가 가능하다.
bear_case: 성장·마진·자본배분이 정상화되고 핵심 불확실성이 불리하게 전개되면 기준 점수보다 낮아질 수 있다.
thesis: Per-share economics are improving and Berkshire still absorbs substantial capital, but the limiting factor is not funding; it is the availability of very large high-return opportunities. Evidence supports strong FCF/share quality but not a 75+ verified incremental ROIC today.

evidence.claim: H1 2026 operating earnings were $24.329B versus $20.801B in H1 2025.
H1 operating cash flow was $21.7B and consolidated capex was $10.6B.
Average B-equivalent shares were 2.1559B in H1 2026 versus 2.1573B in H1 2025.
OxyChem cost about $9.4B and Taylor Morrison about $6.8B equity value.

counterevidence: H1 OCF is affected by insurance/investment working capital and is not a clean owner-FCF measure.
Returns from the 2026 acquisitions are not yet established.
Large T-bill holdings demonstrate unused capital and may signal a constrained reinvestment runway.
unknowns: Post-acquisition ROIC for OxyChem and Taylor Morrison.
Maintenance versus growth capex split at BNSF/BHE.
falsifiers: Incremental returns on major deployments remain below cost of capital for several years.
Per-share operating earnings stagnate while retained capital rises.
Share issuance becomes a persistent source of growth financing.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Average share count declined and Berkshire repurchased shares.
No evidence incremental ROIC has structurally fallen below cost of capital; uncertainty is scored rather than vetoed.

subscores.rationale: Recent acquisitions and capex appear disciplined, but returns on OxyChem/Taylor Morrison are not yet observable and huge scale limits certainty.
Using H1 fallback, capex $10.6B / OCF $21.7B ≈49%, inside the 35–60% observable band; rounded interpolated score ~80.
Operating earnings grew 17% H1 y/y while average B-equivalent shares declined; investment gains are excluded from normalized operating earnings.
